confirmed_facts: Five implement turns reached the 900s Octos turn cap: REQ-2.2, REQ-4.2.1, REQ-6.1.1, REQ-6.1.2 and REQ-6.1.3.
REQ-5.5.2 failed after one tool request with an upstream HTTP 400 proxy_error containing unexpected EOF from api.taotoken.net; it was not an application test failure.
REQ-2.2 had wrote=True and verified=True and its immediate acceptance was 4/4, so the cap did not invalidate the usable state.
REQ-4.2.1 initially reached 6/7; its 589s repair still failed and hit the 10-request guard, then a later shared repair at REQ-4.3.1 reached 8/8.
REQ-6.1.1 had a Name-field fill timeout; two repairs added the create-page route/seed but remained at 12/13 before later shared route work and final recovery.
REQ-6.1.2 had the same Name-field timeout; two repairs remained at 12/13, and a later REQ-6.1.3 repair added draft-save routing and dashboard draft rendering.
REQ-6.1.3 round 0 was an infrastructure failure: /favicon.ico produced ConnectionResetError while the backend was still running; later rounds and the final suite passed.
The 10-request repair guard fired eight independent times; duplicate stdout/stderr lines make sixteen raw log entries.
REQ-6.1.3 and REQ-7.2 selected full rewrite paths after zero-pass infrastructure rounds; REQ-5.6.1 used 106 tools and REQ-6.1.3 used 86 tools.
Postflight reported 196 stray processes, mostly defunct chrome-headless, npm, node, pkill and shell children.
The cgroup memory limit was 2 GiB, peak memory was 1,076,064,256 bytes, and memory.events reported oom=0 and oom_kill=0.
The 51000s global budget was not exhausted: the structured run duration was 16537s, about 32.4% of the budget.
Provider stdout totals were 1272 requests and 40,033,246 total tokens; run.json reports 315,086,357 platform tokens. These are different accounting scopes.
run.json labels 161.881459 with token_cost_currency=CNY while the archive summary describes the same value as USD; the unit conflict remains unresolved.

repair_interpretation.path: 900s cap -> state retained -> immediate 4/4 acceptance; no repair required
900s cap -> 6/7 -> 589s repair and guard -> later REQ-4.3.1 shared server/fixture repair -> 8/8
900s cap -> Name fill timeout -> route and seed repairs without improvement -> later shared implementation -> final pass
900s cap -> Name fill timeout -> two guarded repairs -> later draft-save/dashboard repair -> final pass
900s cap -> favicon ConnectionResetError and 0/13 -> rewrite/repairs -> later 13/13 and final pass

proxy_error.evidence: Provider turn/error and flow logs record HTTP 400 proxy_error, upstream api.taotoken.net and unexpected EOF for REQ-5.5.2; no application assertion ran for that failed turn.

application_or_harness_observations: The favicon reset is a server robustness defect or harness-facing unknown-path handling issue, because the backend remained alive but did not return a response.
The shelf/page/draft locator failures indicate application route/DOM/fixture issues, but exact repair causality is not proven without final diffs and runtime traces.

bottleneck_assessment.primary: Per-turn 900s cap, 10-request repair guard, repeated exploration and process lifecycle leakage.
bottleneck_assessment.memory: Not limiting; peak was about 50.1% of the 2 GiB cgroup limit and no OOM event occurred.
bottleneck_assessment.final_tests: Not limiting; final Playwright completed 34/34, with report duration about 19.3s.

evidence_gaps: No platform build ID, task snapshot ID, commit SHA or upload-to-build binding.
No final generated source diff proving which later repair fixed each inherited node.
No provider retry metadata beyond the recorded proxy error.
No runtime trace proving the exact favicon exception path or initial DOM state.

stage5.recommendation: No action in this phase; preserve the final 34/34 result and treat optimization targets as orchestration/server robustness work only.
